defects.description: The loop `range(1, len(lines) - 1)` contains an off-by-one error that skips the last line of the input text (e.g., if there are 2 lines, it iterates 0 times).
Naive splitting on commas fails to handle standard CSV quoting (e.g., "Field, with comma"), which will be incorrectly split into multiple fields.
Using `text.split('\n')` creates a full list of strings in memory, which is inefficient and potentially dangerous for large 'uploaded spreadsheets'.
Splitting specifically on '\n' will leave trailing carriage return characters ('\r') if the input uses Windows-style CRLF line endings.
Mandatory `.strip()` on every field prevents the ingestion of CSV data where leading/trailing whitespace is syntactically significant.
The check `if not lines` is unreachable because `str.split` always returns a list containing at least one string, even for empty input.
Using `zip(header, cells)` silently discards data if a row contains more fields than the header row.

obvious_bugs: Skips the last row of data due to the range limit.
Fails to parse any CSV field containing a comma.
notes: This code is a classic example of 'reinventing the wheel' poorly; the Python standard library `csv` module exists specifically to solve all the issues identified here (memory efficiency, CRLF handling, and quoted-field parsing).
